To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
incretins stimulate beta-cell replication via distinct intracellular signalling and transcriptional induction of the G1/S cyclin, cyclin D1, in primary rat islet cells and insulinoma cells.

incretins induce beta-cell replication via multiple signalling pathways, involving the cAMP/PKA pathway, p42 MAP kinase and the PI3 kinase pathway, and that incretin-induced proliferation is dependent on transcriptional induction of the cyclinD1 gene.
incretin-induced pancreatic beta-cell replication involves transcriptional induction via multiple signalling pathways of cyclin D, a key regulatory protein in the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
incretins and beta-cell replication.
the molecular mechanisms of beta-cell replication and how these may be affected by incretins, which may have implications in the treatment of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
the molecular mechanisms underlying incretin-stimulated pancreatic beta-cell replication and the role of incretins in the regulation of beta-cell mass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
incretins, GLP-1 in particular, may have the potential of stimulating beta-cell proliferation in humans.
the incretins GLP-1 (and GIP) have a significant effect on beta-cell proliferation in vitro, but the molecular mechanisms of this effect is still not completely understood.
GLP-1 stimulates beta-cell proliferation by a mechanism which involves the cAMP/PKA-, PI3K- and MAPK-pathways, and that GLP- 1 induces cyclin D1 expression in a PKA-, MAPK- and PI3K-dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
incretins stimulate beta-cell replication via multiple signalling pathways involving cAMP/PKA and PI3K.
GLP-1 increases the beta-cell mass by inducing proliferation of existing beta-cells and by increasing the differentiation of pancreatic duct cells into beta-cells.
the incretins GLP-1/GIP stimulate beta-cell replication through the cAMP/PKA and p42 MAPK pathways and that this is mediated via the transcriptional induction of the cell cycle protein, cyclin D1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
incretins stimulate beta-cell replication by a mechanism which involves activation of the cAMP/PKA pathway, PI3K and p42 MAPK.

incretin stimulation of beta-cell replication involves transcriptional induction via distinct intracellular signalling mechanisms, which may be of importance for future development of beta-cell regenerating drugs.

the incretin hormone, GLP-1 stimulates the replication of pancreatic beta-cells via multiple signalling pathways, one of which involves the induction of the cyclin gene, cyclin D1, which is essential for the transition from G1 to S phase in the cell cycle.
